a2-past-copula.title: Past Tense: To Be (partial)
a2-past-copula.pattern: уыдтӕн (I was) · уыди (he/she/it was) · уыдысты (they were)
a2-past-copula.explanation: "To be" has its own past-tense forms, built on a different stem (уыд-) from the present (у/ис): Ахуыргӕнӕг уыдтӕн (I was a teacher), Фын уыди (it was a dream), Сӕхимӕ уыдысты? (were they at home?).
a2-past-copula.fact: Only three persons of this past-tense paradigm are confirmed so far (I/he-she-it/they) -- the "you" and "we" forms aren't taught yet since a clean confirmed example hasn't turned up.

a2-verbs-more.title: More Verbs in Full Conjugation
a2-verbs-more.pattern: хъусын (to hear) · уынын (to see), conjugated across persons
a2-verbs-more.explanation: More practice with the full present-tense pattern you already know, applied to two more verbs: хъусын (to hear) -> хъусын/хъусыс/хъусы/хъусӕм/хъусут/хъусынц, and уынын (to see) -> уынын/уынис/уыны/уынӕм/уынут/уынынц.
a2-verbs-more.fact: уынын is a great example of the 1sg-equals-infinitive rule in action: on its own it's ambiguous between "to see" and "I see", and only the sentence around it (or a subject pronoun) tells you which.
